name: Table
summary: Presents rows and columns of data — also a comparison table: groups of rows, the row's name pinned while scrolling sideways, the header pinned while scrolling down, the best value marked and a 'differences only' switch. Since 0.28.0 (GAR-16) every cell has tabular figures, so price and year columns line up.

a11y.notes: A comparison is plain HTML with Aurea's skin, so a screen reader gets real table semantics: each item is a <th scope="col">, each row is named by a <th scope="row"> (body text, not a column label), and a group of rows is a <tbody> that opens with a <th scope="rowgroup" colSpan> band. The best value is <td data-best> (bold) and must also say so in TEXT — put a Badge reading 'Best' in the cell: colour alone says nothing to someone who cannot see it (WCAG 1.4.1). differencesOnly hides the rows the page marked <tr data-same> with display:none, so they leave the accessibility tree too; the switch that turns it on belongs to the page. The pinned parts do not move focus or add keys: the scroll box is still the one focusable region it always was.

props.name: caption
props.description: Rendered as a real <caption>, and when it is a string it also becomes the accessible name of the scroll region around the table. Without it the region falls back to "Table".

props.name: stickyHeader
props.description: GAR-13: the header stays at the top of the table's box while the body scrolls inside it — the same name and mechanism as DataGrid. The box gets a ceiling, `--table-max-h` (60vh by default), set in CSS: a box with no ceiling never scrolls inside itself. It pins to the box, not to the page: the box also scrolls sideways, and a sticky element only sticks to its nearest scroll container.

props.name: stickyFirstColumn
props.description: GAR-12: the first column — the name of each row — stays put while the table scrolls sideways, on an opaque background so the rest slides under it, with a hairline at its end. With stickyHeader too, the corner stays above both.

props.name: fit
props.description: GAR-12: the table fits its box, without the 720px minimum that makes a wide table scroll sideways. This is what lets a comparison of TWO items fit a 360px phone with no sideways scroll; which two is the page's choice (a Select above the table).

props.name: differencesOnly
props.description: GAR-12: the 'differences only' view — hides the rows the page marked as identical with <tr data-same>. The table does not compare cells itself; the page knows which rows are equal and owns the switch.

props.name: children
props.description: The <thead> and <tbody>, written by you. This is the presentational table; the one that sorts, filters and pages is DataGrid.

props.name: className
props.description: On the <table>. The wrapper around it is focusable (tabIndex 0) so a table wider than the screen can be scrolled with the keyboard, not only by dragging.
